questions.q: Why does 'OrderDate + 7' work directly on Oracle, without any special function?
options: Because Oracle's DATE type is stored internally as a number, so ordinary arithmetic adds days directly
Because Oracle automatically converts every + into a DATEADD call behind the scenes
Oracle doesn't actually support this syntax
Because + is a comment operator in Oracle, not arithmetic
questions.explain: Oracle's DATE type is internally numeric, so plain arithmetic like + 7 genuinely means '7 days later.'

questions.q: What is the correct T-SQL function to add 7 days to a date column?
options: DATEADD(day, 7, OrderDate)
OrderDate + 7
DATE_ADD(OrderDate, INTERVAL 7 DAY)
OrderDate + INTERVAL '7 days'
questions.explain: T-SQL requires DATEADD() with a datepart argument; it has no direct + arithmetic on dates like Oracle does.

questions.q: What is MySQL's function for adding an interval to a date?
options: DATE_ADD(OrderDate, INTERVAL 7 DAY)
DATEADD(day, 7, OrderDate)
ADD_MONTHS(OrderDate, 7)
OrderDate + 7
questions.explain: MySQL uses DATE_ADD(date, INTERVAL n unit) to add a time interval to a date.

questions.q: What does PostgreSQL require that Oracle doesn't, when doing direct date arithmetic like adding 7 days?
options: An explicit INTERVAL literal (e.g. INTERVAL '7 days'), since PostgreSQL distinguishes DATE and INTERVAL types more strictly
A call to DATEADD()
Nothing — PostgreSQL doesn't support date arithmetic at all
A cast to VARCHAR first
questions.explain: PostgreSQL supports direct +/- arithmetic on dates, but requires an explicit INTERVAL literal rather than a bare number like Oracle allows.

questions.q: Why does Oracle provide ADD_MONTHS() and MONTHS_BETWEEN() instead of just letting you add a number of months directly?
options: Because a 'month' isn't a fixed number of days, so simple arithmetic can't represent month-based math the way day-based + does
Because Oracle doesn't support any date arithmetic at all
Because months aren't tracked internally by Oracle's DATE type
Because ADD_MONTHS is deprecated and should never be used
questions.explain: Since months vary in length, Oracle provides dedicated functions (ADD_MONTHS, MONTHS_BETWEEN) rather than relying on fixed-day arithmetic for month-based calculations.
